| [CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md) | Sections over contexts that do not overlap always glue, so a sense that differs between disjoint contexts is not a gluing failure: a failure needs an overlap carrying sections that disagree, and which families count as covers decides whether anything glues | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-088](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-088.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). The sheaf condition says a family of sections that agree on overlaps glues to one global section. Where two contexts do not overlap, agreement is vacuous and they glue. | [CLAIM-219](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-219.md) v4 | A change in the global compatibility of a fixed scenario is either a change in contextuality proper, which the behavioural data read show none of, or a change in overlap consistency, which is ordinary context dependence and moves by at most 2ε when each context moves by ε | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. If pragmatic data are noncontextual as a rule, [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md)'s defeat condition is met by default; what is left to change is overlap consistency, which is the "trivial sense of contextuality" and is fixed by the local distributions. The only instance of the headline is the stipulated [CASE-037](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-037.md). Among the claims [LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md) is cited only by [CLAIM-041](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-041.md), not by [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md). The objection is open; it does not say a contextual pragmatic data set cannot exist. | Active |
| [CLAIM-220](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-220.md) v2 | For a named population of receivers and a stated family of tasks, what survives a translation, retelling or rendering is the set of task-relevant communicative distinctions those receivers can still recover from it, and measured preservation of the pragmatic observables predicts that recovery better than preservation of the wording or of the proposition, with or without its force | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to the audit's objections to the tests of the manuscript's thesis ([CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md), [CLAIM-232](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-232.md), [CLAIM-243](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-243.md), [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md), [CLAIM-226](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-226.md), [CLAIM-222](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md)). It supersedes [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md), by the owner's delegated ruling of 2026-10-29. It is a proposal, not a finding. It does not claim the line's distinctive machinery is needed: that is [CLAIM-202](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-202.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-221](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-221.md) | The relational-constitution thesis's defeat condition describes a standard rival the record holds no counter for, intention-based accounts of illocution, which plausibly meet it for every act in the four-speakers case except the institutional one | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) is defeated by a held account that individuates teasing, reproach and reprimand by the utterance plus speaker-internal states. That is the intention-based line of Grice, Strawson and Bach and Harnish, none of whom the record holds. On it [CASE-018](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-018.md)'s friend, parent and comedian differ in communicative intention, and only the judge needs norms, which Searle ([LIT-482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-482.md)) already supplies. The record's own model for [CLAIM-111](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-111.md) is of this family. The objection is open; it would narrow [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) to institutional acts unless an argument from uptake meets it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-222](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md) v2 | No design in the programme includes an interlingual translation, and the defeat conditions are disjunctive, so English retellings and model chains could settle a thesis about what survives translation | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens). The workbench entry for 2026-10-10 notes that the title's question "is left with no translated text in the programme"; no CLAIM says it, and none draws the consequence. Every stimulus set the designs name is English, or names no language; Villon→Henley and Marot→Hofstadter never enter a design. | [CLAIM-223](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-223.md) v2 | Whether a distinction survived is fixed by what the receivers can recover, and whether it can be shown to have survived is fixed by what the analyst's probes can identify, so the manuscript's thesis and the October fidelity clause, read so, answer different parts of one question | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-211](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-211.md), and the argument [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md) asked for: "the thesis now needs both conditions, or an argument for dropping one". On [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md)'s cases: a distinction identifiable but unusable did not survive for those receivers; one usable but unidentifiable survived without evidence of it. Read so, `complements` is right on content. A proposal: it is a reading of [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md), not what A218 says. | Active |
| [CLAIM-224](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-224.md) | Under partial relational constitution, a translation always changes the participants, audience and norms that the relational-constitution thesis makes constituents of the act, so whether the act survives turns on a correspondence of relations the structure cannot supply from inside | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. A translation is addressed to a new audience under new norms, so on [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) it changes constituents of the act, and the record's way out is always a correspondence ("the appropriate relationships", "corresponding relational organizations"). That makes [QUESTION-005](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md) a question about what the act is, not only how to measure it, and the record's model of translation holds the audience fixed. [CLAIM-138](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-138.md) spares [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md); this applies its point to [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) through translation. The objection is open. It does not say acts never survive translation. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-225](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-225.md) v4 | Blackwell's order measures what an ideal decision-maker could do, not what a given receiver can reconstruct, and the line's claims that a rendering can improve access describe garblings that real receivers do better with, which is the shape of the Blackwell thesis's own defeat condition | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange connects the two claims. A generator that sees only the text makes its image a garbling of the text about the situation, so by Blackwell's theorem the image is no better for any decision. [CLAIM-087](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-087.md) says such an image can improve access. Either that effect is impossible, or judged access is not Blackwell informativeness, and then [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s standard is not the one [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md)'s receiver and its defeat condition use. It meets the shape of [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s defeat condition, not its letter. It is distinct from [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md), which sets the analyst against the receiver: this sets the ideal receiver against an actual one. | Active |
| [CLAIM-226](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-226.md) v2 | The defeat tests pool unnamed judges and treat their disagreement as noise, though the theory makes the act partly constituted by its audience; for historical sources there is no source audience at all, and for interlingual ones population differences are read as distortion | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. A theory on which the act depends on its audience predicts structured variation between judges, so averaging a convenience sample measures an unnamed population's act. The source term of D(τ) for Villon, Henley or Marot can only be a modern reading, and for a live interlingual case the source and target judges are different communities, so the distance confounds population with transport. [CLAIM-074](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-074.md) says fidelity differs across interpreters, as a thesis; it is not applied to the tests. It does not say cross-population fidelity is meaningless. | Active |
| [CLAIM-227](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-227.md) | No validated measure of footing or stance exists in the record, and the one repeated assignment of footing, the analyst's own, changed between passes | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Footing and stance are the observables the central theses turn on, yet the only footing judgement made twice of the same texts, the assistant's labelling of its own four refrains, changed between A38 and A39 without comment ([CASE-012](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-012.md)), and no design gives judges a definition, a response format, a reliability target or a validation against a known contrast. Granted, because it is a reading of the record. It does not say footing cannot be measured. | Active |
| [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md) v4 | D_obs restated over a rendering procedure, with one kernel family fitted on some source items and scored on held-out ones and the target term the readers' response averaged over the procedure's output, separates rendering procedures that receivers' task-indexed recovery separates, so restated it measures observational fidelity informatively | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, of the manuscript's L_obs and the profile's D_obs after [CLAIM-207](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md), [CLAIM-230](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md) and [CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md). For one pair a constant kernel makes D_obs zero ([CLAIM-207](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md)); fixed across items, it fits only if the target readers' responses do not vary with the item. The repair ties the outcome-level kernels to the text channel, makes the transport a property of a procedure ([CLAIM-230](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md)), and makes deficiency a finite computation over judgement outcomes ([CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md)). A proposal: the derivation is elementary, but whether the restated measure is informative is the defeat condition's empirical question. It does not say a fitted kernel is the translator's process. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-229](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-229.md) v3 | The footing, compensation and constitution theses ground on invented cases whose readings the assistant assigned, and the case filed for the proposition's non-necessity holds the words fixed, so it shows only insufficiency | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-061](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-061.md), [CLAIM-091](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-091.md), [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) and [CLAIM-084](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-084.md) list fictional cases in `grounds`, which [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) makes evidence, while the cases' own bodies say they show a possibility, and [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md)'s defeat condition asks a rival to predict a variation nobody observed. [CASE-018](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-018.md), filed as the necessity half of [CLAIM-061](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-061.md), keeps the words fixed, so it shows only that the proposition is not sufficient. Granted: it is a reading of the record. It does not say the theses are false or that invented cases are useless. | Superseded — by [ARG-021](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-021.md), [ARG-020](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-020.md), [ARG-013](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-013.md), [ARG-024](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-024.md), [ARG-039](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-039.md) |
| [CLAIM-230](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md) v3 | Blackwell comparison needs the state each rendering is about, which natural texts do not supply, so a decision measure is fixed by whoever labels the state, and it orders translation procedures, not single renderings | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Testing Blackwell's order needs the joint law of the situation and the signal. For natural texts the situation is what interpretation recovers, so it comes from the stimulus design, the analyst's labels or the judges, and decision-relevant information is measured against whoever fixed it. An experiment is a family of distributions, one per state, so a single rendering of a single poem is not one. [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s defeat condition, "one rendering is a garbling of another", is then not well typed. It does not say a design-based state is illegitimate. | Active |
| [CLAIM-231](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-231.md) | On observed responses, a rendering that keeps the response distribution of each order of two framings within ε of the source's, under an outcome correspondence, keeps the observed order effect within 2ε, a bound identified from data, while the intertwining identity bounds it only through defects of an unidentified state model | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, after [CLAIM-253](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-253.md). The commutator identity of the manuscript's §9 holds, and its defects are not identified from data, by the objection's hidden-bit construction. What can be estimated is the response distribution under each order, so the bound is restated on those: a special case of observational distortion with contexts indexed by framing order. Active, because it is elementary and checkable. It does not say the state-model account is wrong, and it does not identify the defects. | Active |
| [CLAIM-232](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-232.md) v3 | Human ratings of stance or footing and human ratings of fidelity of the same renderings share rater construal, scale use and a general impression, which a machine similarity score shares with neither | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Ratings of stance and footing share rater construal, scale use and the reading of one stimulus with ratings of fidelity, and an embedding score shares none of that. The manuscript's split annotators (§10, as [QUESTION-005](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md) reports) remove the shared rater, not the shared construal. It is a second reason, beside [CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md), that the central tests are easy to pass. Open, because a design could answer it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md) v2 | The central theses' defeat conditions pit them only against embedding, propositional or surface similarity, and every rival account the record names (functional equivalence, Gutt's interpretive resemblance, speech-act pragmatics) also predicts that judged pragmatic observables beat text similarity | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure and empirical lenses); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-023](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-023.md) says the pragmatic point is not new, and a functional-equivalence, relevance-theoretic or speech-act account passes the same test. Granted, because it is read off the texts. It does not say the theses are false, only that their stated tests cannot separate them from the positions they claim to improve on. | Active |
| [CLAIM-234](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-234.md) v3 | The record's iterated-learning readings bear on lexical, structural and functional transmission, and none measures stance, footing or speech-act function along a chain | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Bartlett is unread, and the transmission-chain work on social and affective content is not in the record. Granted: it is a reading of the record. It is minor because [CLAIM-068](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-068.md) is off the central chains, and it does not say stances are not stabilized by transmission. | Superseded — by [ARG-027](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-027.md) |
| [CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md) v3 | The line's proposed quantities have no finite-data estimators: plug-in signalling from one or a few occurrences per context is positive in expectation when the true marginals agree, so the contextual fraction is undefined on raw tables, and deficiency over text-valued renderings has no estimator | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal and empirical lenses); no turn of the exchange raises it. The plug-in signalling of two empirical marginals is positive in expectation when the true marginals agree, so raw tables signal, and the contextual fraction is undefined on them. With one occurrence per context, a non-signalling rank-2 system gives Δ of 0, 2 or 4, with expectation 2: the values [NOTE-654](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-654.md) finds in 51 of the 90 systems behind [CLAIM-125](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-125.md)'s "69 of the 90 systems signal". The data are author-assigned corpus senses, not judgements. Deficiency over text-valued renderings has no estimator. It does not say signalling is rare in pragmatic judgements, where order effects are themselves signalling. | Active |
| [CLAIM-236](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-236.md) v2 | Under the rational-speech-act model the distribution-over-situations thesis grounds on, a form's interpretation depends on what else the speaker could have said, so matching source and target posteriors needs a correspondence of alternative sets that translation changes and no entry names | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-111](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-111.md) makes a translation faithful when the target's posterior over communicative situations matches the source's, and its worked model, [THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md), makes that posterior depend on the set of alternative utterances. A translation replaces the source language's alternatives with the target's, so a rendering with the same literal content can carry a different posterior. Granted, because it follows from the model as the record states it. It does not say the model is wrong or [CLAIM-111](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-111.md) false. | Rejected |
| [CLAIM-237](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-237.md) v2 | The first open problem of directed transport is not yet posed: a contextual model is a menu of incompatible experiments, and under the natural order on menus any state-independent classical simulation is dominated automatically, so what is open is only the converse or a deficiency bound | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Blackwell's order compares experiments, each a family of distributions over one parameter. An empirical model has no parameter, and if it is contextual it has no joint distribution, only one per context. Posing [CLAIM-125](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-125.md)'s first part needs models indexed by situations and an order on menus of experiments. Under the natural order, the preservation direction is automatic for a classical simulation that does not depend on the situation. Granted, because the argument is elementary. It narrows what is open; it does not close it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-238](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-238.md) v2 | Many of the line's defeat conditions cannot in practice be met: the comparative ones are null results with no margin over an observable set the thesis may re-choose, and the possibility theses' are universal negatives that no finite study establishes | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange raises it, though [CASE-029](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-029.md) records the decision rules that were dropped. Three shapes of defeat condition cannot be met. "As well as" is a null result, which needs an equivalence margin and power, and no entry states either. The observables are "not fixed in advance" ([CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md)). And the "can" theses are defeated only by "never" or "always", so one construction confirms them and no study refutes them, while what the main thesis needs from them is prevalence and magnitude, which none states. Granted: each point is read off the texts. It does not say the theses are false or untestable in principle. | Active |
| [CLAIM-239](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-239.md) | A defeat condition that says something cannot be done is met by an argument that it cannot, not by a record of failures, so the admissibility and correspondence theses can fail by their own conditions, though no study the programme runs can make them fail | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to the fourth point of [CLAIM-238](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-238.md). luria.yaml's blurb for `defeated_if` is "what would defeat the thesis — a kind of result or argument". [CLAIM-077](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-077.md)'s condition and [CLAIM-143](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-143.md)'s second disjunct ("[QUESTION-005](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md) answered negatively") are met by a showing that the distinctions or correspondences cannot be fixed independently. What the objection gets right is that no finite study meets them, so the programme's experiments do not test these two theses; argument does. Active, because it is read off the rule. | Active |
| [CLAIM-240](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-240.md) v2 | A holistic fidelity judgement is fidelity under the judges' default task, a weighting of the profile's components that can be estimated on some renderings and tested on others, so it is well defined and consistent with task-relativity, and a defeat condition that uses it must name the population and fix the weighting before the test | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md). Task-relativity ([CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md)) denies a ranking that holds across tasks, not that a population has a default task. A weighting estimated on held-in data and tested on held-out data is a finding, not a fit, and a weighting fixed before the test leaves no room to blame the task after a failure. A proposal: whether holistic judgements are such a weighting is itself empirical. The objection is right that the stated defeat conditions name neither task nor receivers; [CLAIM-220](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-220.md), [CLAIM-204](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md) and [QUESTION-075](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-075.md) address that. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-241](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-241.md) v2 | Partial constitution by uptake makes competent participants' uptake a defeasible standard of a communicative kind, not the criterion: where the act's other constituents, such as its institutional conditions, diverge from how even informed participants take it, their verdicts can be wrong, and a standard must say whose competence counts, for which class of acts, and how divided verdicts are combined, which a majority does not | The interlocutor's first refinement at U62 (A240), with its row on [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md), pressed at full strength. [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md) moves from "partly constituted by ... expected uptake" to "the judges ... are the criterion". Partial constitution gives uptake a vote, not the last word, so where the act's other constituents diverge from informed uptake the verdicts can be wrong. The claim also names no rule for combining divided verdicts and no class of acts. Open: answering it means saying whether a defeasible standard re-opens the horn [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md) closed. It does not say uptake is not a standard. | Active |
| [CLAIM-242](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-242.md) v2 | The use-level counterpart of Saussure's value is an utterance's contrast with the alternatives its speaker could have used in context; values do not cross between languages, which is why fidelity is graded transport through an anchored correspondence rather than identity of value | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-254](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-254.md). It grants the objection's premises: value is internal to one language state, and it is a fact of langue, while the line's observables are facts of use. It denies the conclusion. What the premise rules out is identity of value across languages, which the line does not claim ([CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)), and transport through a correspondence fixed from outside both systems is what [CLAIM-082](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-082.md)'s own qualification already requires. At the level of use, contrast with alternatives is the rational-speech-act model's premise ([THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md)) and Bergen, Goodman and Levy's finding ([LIT-809](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-809.md)). Saussure becomes precedent, not premise. A proposal, not a refutation. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-243](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-243.md) v2 | Read as description, the manuscript's thesis is close to true by definition; read as a criterion, it is a schema until the decision family Q is fixed, and its descriptive defeat condition can test neither reading | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. A distinction no receiver can recover has not survived for anyone, so the descriptive reading is near-analytic. The normative reading leaves which distinctions count to the task family Q, which [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md)'s summary calls "normative and contestable". The defeat condition fixes observables the thesis declines to fix, and tests them descriptively: [CLAIM-085](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-085.md)'s split of normative from descriptive, applied to the thesis rather than to model judges. It does not say the thesis is empty. | Active |
| [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md) v2 | The defeat tests take one holistic, task-free judgement of fidelity as ground truth, though the line's own theses say fidelity is task-relative, interpreter-relative and not a single ranking | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. A judge asked "how faithful?" or "the same kind?" supplies an unstated task and weighting, and is one interpreter. The theory's measure must then be fitted to that weighting, which is circular, or a mismatch blamed on the judges' task, which leaves nothing that defeats. It does not say the judgements are useless, only that the defeat conditions lack the task and receiver index the line's own theses say fidelity needs. [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md) is its neighbour: that one moves the criterion to the analyst, and neither says it is task-free. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-245](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-245.md) | Under Contextuality-by-Default, a deterministic context-wise recoding can make a noncontextual signalling source maximally contextual, or turn a contextual source into pure signalling, so per-content signalling is not monotone under such maps and the quantity to bound is joint overlap discrepancy | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Two worked rank-2 systems answer [NOTE-654](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-654.md)'s open question negatively: [THEORY-177](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-177.md)'s per-content signalling can rise under deterministic recodings, once the source signals, and CbD contextuality can be created or removed by them. By data processing, the joint overlap discrepancy cannot rise, so that is the quantity [CLAIM-125](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-125.md)'s second part should name. Granted, because the examples are elementary. It does not say [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md) is wrong, which is about no-signalling models. | Active |
| [CLAIM-246](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-246.md) v2 | Sharing a kind is symmetric and blind to which work is the source, so the October thesis cannot say a translation is of its original, against the line's own directed, graded fidelity and identity through descent | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-137](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-137.md) makes realizations one act by a shared invariant, "not resemblance to an original", and [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)'s defeat condition tests judgements of shared kind. Sharing a kind is symmetric and says nothing of descent, so an utterance made independently of the source, of the same kind, scores as a translation does. The line's own theses make fidelity directed and graded ([CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)) and identity partly a matter of transmission ([CLAIM-002](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-002.md)). The objection is open; it does not say descent must be part of fidelity, only that the kind criterion cannot state it. | Rejected |
| [CLAIM-247](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-247.md) v3 | The bearer of communicative identity reversed, from an operational object defined on observed responses to a kind that can outrun observation, and no turn argues the change; both stances stand in the record | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. It is [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md)'s point for the bearer of identity rather than the receiver. The manuscript defined the communicative object on observations, and [CLAIM-112](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-112.md) says that was "a choice of what to measure, not a theory of what meaning is". Three results the record already holds. [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md): capture in the operator model needs both arrows of [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s circuit, and scoring operators independently of the dominant interpretation removes it. [CLAIM-141](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-141.md): a loop always has a distributional fixed point, so what binds it is a constraint that prescribes marginals. [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) ([NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md)): an active-inference agent locks in with action available, because its own sampling policy withholds the evidence that would correct it. The claim does not say action is unimportant, only that it is not what does the anchoring. | Active |
| [CLAIM-350](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-350.md) v2 | A coarse-graining preserves a deterministic judgment exactly when the judgment is constant on its fibres: the judgment then factors through the coarse description, uniquely on its image, and otherwise two states the judgment tells apart have been merged | A21 §3 and §18 (Candidate 1) of the exchange of 2026-10-17, and A22's Construction A: for a judgment J and a coarse-graining C on the same states, J = j∘C for some j exactly when C(x₁) = C(x₂) implies J(x₁) = J(x₂). Granted, because it is elementary (the universal property of a quotient) and Ak's; the proof is in the body. It is [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md)'s judgment-valued special case with the converse added: [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) says a partition sufficient for one target need not be for another, and this says which partitions serve a deterministic judgment, those whose fibres lie inside its level sets, so the coarsest is the judgment's own partition. The sharp edge: it says when a description keeps a judgment, never whether the judgment is right. A21's probabilistic and causal versions are recorded in the body, not claimed. | Active |
| [CLAIM-380](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-380.md) v2 | With finitely many states and finitely many outcomes, the positive part of the Bayes-risk increase on the same decision problem is directed, is zero from a garbling back to its source, vanishes for every finite problem and prior exactly when the rendering is at least as informative as the source, and has A86's D_Q as its symmetrization | The finite-outcome part of [CLAIM-326](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-326.md). Define D⁺_Q(U → V; π) = sup over q in Q of [r_q,π(V) − r_q,π(U)]⁺, with losses in [0, 1] and a stated prior. A garbling never gains. The term is directed. A86's D_Q is its symmetrization. And with every finite problem and prior, it vanishes exactly when V is at least as informative as U, by Blackwell's Theorem 6 ([THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md)). It does not cover outcome spaces that are not finite, or say this is the right decision term. | Active |
| [CLAIM-381](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-381.md) | Over a finite class of items with finite judgement outcomes, a constant outcome kernel fits every item only when the target readers' averaged responses do not vary with the item, an exact fit is a garbling with the item as common parameter, and Le Cam's deficiency and its restriction to finitely many decision problems are finite computations | The derivational core of [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md). Over a finite class of items, the target term is the readers' response averaged over a procedure's output, and one outcome kernel family is fixed across the items. Then a constant kernel fits only target responses that carry no information about the item. An exact fit is a garbling, with the item as the common parameter. And Le Cam's deficiency between the two finite tables is one linear programme. Its restriction to finitely many decision problems is a finite computation. It does not say the measure is informative, which is [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md)'s empirical question. | Active |

| [CLAIM-450](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-450.md) v5 | Three standards for a communicative distinction come apart: statistical distinguishability of an interpreter's response profiles, measured locally by the Fisher metric and never raised by a parameter-independent garbling; usability by a bounded receiver, which a transformation can raise; and pragmatic efficacy in the act; and where response models are singular, as Watanabe's theory treats, a missing response can come from an absent attempt or an unresponsive receiver alike, and only intervention or later dynamics separate them | The owner's, 2026-10-24, after setting aside the belief–knowledge distinction: "forget about that distinction then and let's connect back to the communicative act stuff and amari/watanabe theory". | [CLAIM-458](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-458.md) | A reception split between populations with unequal access to the source is partly a difference of access and not of weighting, so a default task's weights can be estimated only on the components every population compared can perceive | The limit [CLAIM-240](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-240.md)'s note of 2026-10-10 recorded and did not code, filed as an objection. | [CLAIM-461](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-461.md) | Compensation is not only a re-performance notion: for a reader whose code gives the literal word a meaning the source lacked, the compensating rendering can be the more faithful report, so assigning compensation to re-performance alone needs narrowing | The narrowing [CLAIM-212](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-212.md)'s note of 2026-10-10 proposed and did not make, filed as an objection so it can carry a status.
